item.anchor.thermometer.use: Use it on a block or in the air to read the temperature
item.anchor.thermometer.sneak: Sneak and use it on a block to record it over time
message.anchor.thermometer.waiting: No reading yet: this area is still being loaded into the simulation
item.anchor.thermal_camera.use: Use it to switch between surfaces and air
item.anchor.thermal_camera.sneak: Sneak and use it to lock the scale
message.anchor.thermal_camera.nothing: Nothing in view is simulated yet
message.anchor.probe.full: A dimension holds at most %s probes; remove one with /anchor probe remove
message.anchor.probe.bad_name: Probe names are letters, digits, _ and -, at most %s of them
message.anchor.laboratory.air: The air here stays at %s and %s humidity, the sun gives no heat, and nothing spawns or grows, so only your experiments change what you build.
message.anchor.laboratory.instruments: Use the thermometer on a block to read it, or sneak and use it to record it; hold the thermal camera to see heat.
message.anchor.laboratory.commands: %s lists ready-made experiments to build, %s pauses, steps and speeds up heat, and %s saves your own experiments so that you can run them again.
experiment.anchor.cooling.summary: A block of iron at 1227 °C cools in still air. Its glow fades from orange through dull red to nothing in about five minutes.
experiment.anchor.cooling.watch: Its top cools faster than its middle: the surface radiates heat and warms the air around it, while the inside must first conduct its heat out to the surface. Hold the thermal camera to watch it cool.
experiment.anchor.conduction.summary: Rods of copper, iron, stone and brick stand on lava. Copper carries the heat to its top first, iron follows, and stone and brick barely warm at the top.
experiment.anchor.conduction.watch: The probes at the tops of the rods record the race. Hold the thermal camera to see the heat climb each rod.
experiment.anchor.melting.summary: Ice and stone at -10 °C warm side by side on copper hot plates over lava. The stone warms on past 0 °C; the ice stops there until it has melted.
experiment.anchor.melting.watch: Ice and stone take in heat much alike, so their lines run together until the ice reaches 0 °C. Then the heat goes into melting it rather than warming it: that heat is the latent heat of fusion.
experiment.anchor.insulation.summary: Three blocks of iron at 150 °C: one bare, one wrapped in glass and one wrapped in wool. The bare one cools fastest, and the wool keeps its iron hot for hours.
experiment.anchor.insulation.watch: Wool is mostly trapped air and conducts heat almost 30 times worse than glass. The bare iron is held in the air, so that it touches nothing.
message.anchor.experiment.list: Ready-made experiments, which operators build in front of them with /anchor experiment build <name>:
message.anchor.experiment.unknown: There is no experiment called %s; %s names them.
message.anchor.experiment.outside: There is no room for %s between the bottom and the top of the world here.
message.anchor.experiment.not_simulated: Heat does not run in all of the space %s needs yet: wait a moment after arriving and try again.
message.anchor.experiment.blocked: %s needs a clear space %s blocks wide, %s deep and %s tall in front of you, and %s is in the way at %s.
message.anchor.experiment.unheld: %s needs solid ground under its bench to hold the %s in it, and there is none at %s.
message.anchor.experiment.not_started: A block of it could not be given its starting temperature.
message.anchor.experiment.not_saved: It could not be saved as a snapshot, so it cannot be run again with /anchor snapshot restore.
message.anchor.experiment.probes: Probes record it as it runs: %s.
message.anchor.experiment.chart: Probes record it as it runs: %s. The chart you were given keeps drawing what they record.
message.anchor.experiment.paused: Heat is paused here, so nothing happens yet; %s lets it run.
message.anchor.experiment.speed: Speed heat up to see the result within minutes: %s, and %s to go back.
message.anchor.experiment.again: %s runs it again from the start.
